title: Upper bound on the sample count
statement: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the number of samples prescribed per coefficient by the exact-degree estimator, viewed as a rational number, is at most $4B/\varepsilon^2$, where $B$ is the failure-bit count at the confidence parameter assigned to the family of subsets of $[n]$ of size at most $k$, and $\varepsilon$ is the estimator's degree-$k$ accuracy parameter.
